ingredients.item: A pinch of salt and ground pepper
scallion , sliced; a pinch of gochugaru , optional

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Oil at medium-high, garlic in for 30 seconds of blonding, then the pressed zucchini in one layer as much as the pan allows — 2 minutes undisturbed for the first side.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the cut faces gold against the green skin, and the pan sizzles steadily rather than hissing out steam — the draw did its work. If the pan floods with liquid, the press was skipped; pour it off, accept a softer bowl, salt earlier next time.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Toss or turn, 2–3 minutes more — the zucchini should stay crisp-shouldered with gilded edges, not collapse.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the bend test: a half-moon bends with a spine of resistance. Fully limp zucchini is over; this bowl's identity is the last of the crunch.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Off the heat: soy, pepper, sesame oil, seeds, scallion, gochugaru if using — the residual heat blooms them without cooking them away.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test with rice: sesame-garlic first, the zucchini's sweet green core, a clean finish. It should taste like the vegetable decided to dress up, not like dressing looking for a vegetable.

visualDonenessCues: the cut faces gold against the green skin, and the pan sizzles steadily rather than hissing out steam — the draw did its work. If the pan floods with liquid, the press was skipped; pour it off, accept a softer bowl, salt earlier next time.
the bend test: a half-moon bends with a spine of resistance. Fully limp zucchini is over; this bowl's identity is the last of the crunch.
the eating test with rice: sesame-garlic first, the zucchini's sweet green core, a clean finish. It should taste like the vegetable decided to dress up, not like dressing looking for a vegetable.
storageNotes: Best the day it's made; acceptable at a day refrigerated, re-panned for 60 seconds. The raw salted half-moons hold half a day in the fridge, ready to finish.

Variations: matchstick carrot added at the sear for color; a spoon of ssamjang (#SA01) thinned into the pan for the deep-flavored fork; the same build on mushrooms or snap peas carries the method anywhere.
